'As an additional cost to play this, you MAY charge your hero's soul. If a YELLOW card is charged this way, this gets OVERPOWER.'

The gate was authored correctly -- the CHARGE cost stamps the charged card's colour on the card being played, and CHARGED_THIS_WAY reads it -- but it hung off a PLAY ability, which loader.conditional_keywords cannot see, so the printed Overpower applied unconditionally and charging nothing still gave overpower.

THE COST MOVED TO CARD LEVEL and that is load-bearing. interpreter._run_ability CHECKS AND PAYS an ability's additional_costs on every dispatch, and a WHILE_STATIC is dispatched on every attack-power recalculation -- so leaving the cost here would charge the soul repeatedly through one combat. The card-level `cost` is checked for legality and paid once (play.py, _dsl_cd.play_cost). An optional additional cost never blocks the play either way.

What was charged is settled while paying, so reading the condition continuously (CR 6.2.3d) gives the same answer as reading it once.
